data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash -l
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --gres=gpu:v100:1
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=1
#   --time=00:15:00
#   --job-name=GPU_matmul
#   --output=log.matmul_%j.out
#   --account NTDD0002
#   --partition=dav
#   --reservation=casper_8xV100

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=15m
#flux: --job-name=GPU_matmul

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:v100:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU (or without a V100), causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm options: --account NTDD0002, --partition=dav, --reservation=casper_8xV100
# Flux accounting/queue/reservation selection are site-specific; no portable equivalents.
# Performance implication: job may be charged differently, may not land on the intended GPU nodes/reservation, increasing queue time or preventing access.

# Omitted Slurm option: --output=log.matmul_%j.out
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose a unique filename.

module purge
module load ncarenv/1.2
module load nvhpc/20.11
module list

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${NCAR_ROOT_CUDA}/lib64:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}
echo ${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}
nvidia-smi

export PCAST_COMPARE=abs=6,summary

echo -e "\nBeginning code output:\n-------------\n"

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, run within the allocation (optionally via flux run -n 1).
./matmul.exe

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 V100 GPU (`--gres=gpu:v100:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job constrained placement via partition/reservation (`--partition=dav`, `--reservation=casper_8xV100`) but the Flux resource section has no equivalent constraints; the job may not run on the intended hardware or within the intended reservation.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash -l
# Batch directives
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:v100:1
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --account NTDD0002
#SBATCH --partition=dav
#SBATCH --reservation=casper_8xV100
#SBATCH --time=00:15:00
#SBATCH --output=log.matmul_%j.out
#SBATCH --job-name=GPU_matmul

# Load the necessary modules (software)
module purge
module load ncarenv/1.2
module load nvhpc/20.11
module list

# Update LD_LIBRARY_PATH so that cuda libraries can be found
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${NCAR_ROOT_CUDA}/lib64:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}
echo ${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}
nvidia-smi

export PCAST_COMPARE=abs=6,summary

# Move to the correct directory and run the executable
echo -e "\nBeginning code output:\n-------------\n"
srun ./matmul.exe
